chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), in [a hadith]:

Regarding a man who divorced his wife with a revocable divorce (Talaq Raj'i), then her husband died, she said: She observes the waiting period (Iddah) of the nearer of the two periods, which is four months and ten days.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a woman whose husband dies while they are in a revocable divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the legal principle of 'Aqra al-Ajalayn' (taking the longer of the two periods) for a woman in revocable divorce whose husband dies, establishing that she must observe the full four months and ten days rather than the shorter three menstrual cycles. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that the death of the husband during the revocable phase triggers the full widowhood waiting period, ensuring clarity in inheritance and remarriage eligibility. The narration underscores the precision of early Shia jurists in distinguishing between the transitional state of Talaq Raj'i and the finality of death.
